result.note: Mostly a political spat; tested only the durable facts on India's three licensed satellite broadband operators and their regulatory status.

questions.prompt: In October 2026, the Ministry of Communications responded to a claim that Starlink was being unfairly blocked in India. Consider the following statements about satellite broadband operators in India at that time:
items: All three licensed satellite operators had been assigned spectrum and had begun commercial operations.
The Ministry said security assessments were under way for each of the licensed satellite operators.
Eutelsat OneWeb, one of the licensed operators, is backed by Bharti Airtel.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is wrong because Starlink, Eutelsat OneWeb and Reliance's Jio-SES venture were all still awaiting spectrum assignment and final clearances before commercial launch. The Ministry called the suggestion of a discriminatory framework baseless and said all three were at broadly the same stage.
questions.source: Starlink, Bharti Airtel-backed Eutelsat OneWeb, and Reliance's Jio-SES venture still await spectrum assignment and final clearances before launching commercial operations
